correctness.rationale: For odd N at most one cyclic gap exceeds N/2, so the endpoints can be cyclically labeled with opposite paired gaps a,c<N/2. Their pair sums have positive lengths 2cos(πa/N), 2cos(πc/N) and direction difference π+π(b-d)/N. The squared norm therefore equals four times the sum of the squared cosine difference and the nonnegative direction-error term. If a≠c, successive cosine drops grow strictly on the relevant interval, and equality needs paired gaps 1 and 2, with b=d. If a=c, odd parity gives b≠d and N-2a≥3. The norm is 4cos(πa/N)|sin(π(b-d)/(2N))|, bounded below by 4sin(3π/(2N))sin(π/(2N)), the same minimum. Equality needs a=c=(N-3)/2 and opposite gaps 1 and 2. Both cases give the cyclic word (1,m,2,m); its reversal is a rotation and it has no proper period, even at N=5. For even N a zero sum pairs antipodes: a prescribed nonzero sum of two unit vectors determines the unordered pair, so the pair summing to its negative is the negated pair; when the pair sum is zero both pairs are already antipodal. This includes N=4. The stated normalization, Taylor constant and equality reindexing at a unit k all follow.

Only the analytic argument proves the all-order classification; no formal or expert certification is claimed.
